newsitem.title: FRANCE: New bomb blast in Corsica -- no one hurt.
newsitem.headline: New bomb blast in Corsica -- no one hurt.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded late on Friday outside government offices in the north Corsican town of Corte causing widespread damage but no casualties, police said.
No one was hurt in the attack and the identity of those responsible was not immediately established.

The attack came after Corsican separatists claimed responsibility for three earlier bomb attacks on the French mainland and on their Mediterranean island, and threatened French Air Force planes at one island base.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC-Canal Historique), in a statement to a Bastia radio station, said it bombed the Marseille headquarters of SNCM, the main shipping company serving the French Mediterranean island, on Thursday.
It also bombed the administrative tribunal in Limoges on the mainland on Thursday and an empty mess at the French Air Force's Solenzara base in Corsica on Wednesday.
The blasts caused damage but no injuries.
